title: Strep throat — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: Strep throat is a bacterial infection of the throat and tonsils that commonly causes sudden sore throat, pain on swallowing, fever, and sometimes white patches on the tonsils.

title: Common cold — MedlinePlus (summary)
text: The common cold is a mild viral infection that typically causes runny or stuffy nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, and sometimes low-grade fever; symptoms are usually gradual and self-limiting.

title: Influenza (Flu) — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: Influenza is a viral respiratory illness that often causes sudden high fever, chills, muscle aches, cough, sore throat, headache, and profound fatigue.

title: COVID-19 — WHO (brief)
text: COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2 and commonly presents with fever, dry cough, fatigue, and may include loss of smell or taste; severe cases can cause difficulty breathing.

title: Gastroenteritis — Cleveland Clinic (summary)
text: Gastroenteritis (stomach flu) causes inflammation of the stomach and intestines, leading to nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, and diarrhea, often developing over hours to days.

title: Pneumonia — NIH (summary)
text: Pneumonia is an infection of the lungs that causes cough (often productive), fever, chest pain with breathing, rapid breathing, and shortness of breath; severity varies by cause and patient.

title: Allergic rhinitis — AAFA (summary)
source: Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America
text: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever) produces sneezing, nasal congestion, runny nose, itchy eyes and throat, often triggered by pollen, dust, or pet dander and worsened seasonally.

title: Urinary tract infection — Mayo Clinic (summary)
text: A urinary tract infection commonly causes a frequent urge to urinate, pain or burning during urination, cloudy or strong-smelling urine, and sometimes lower abdominal pain or fever.

title: Appendicitis — NIH (summary)
text: Appendicitis typically causes sudden onset of abdominal pain (often starting near the navel and moving to the lower right), loss of appetite, nausea, and sometimes fever; it often requires urgent evaluation.

title: Migraine — NIH (summary)
text: Migraine is a neurological headache disorder characterized by moderate to severe throbbing head pain, often one-sided, and may include nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light or sound.

title: Severe bleeding / hemorrhage (triage note)
text: Significant uncontrolled bleeding, fainting, or signs of shock (pale skin, rapid pulse) indicate a medical emergency and require immediate emergency care.

title: Dehydration — CDC (summary)
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
text: Dehydration can result from vomiting or diarrhea and causes dizziness, decreased urination, dry mouth, and weakness; severe dehydration is an emergency, especially in children and older adults.
